title: env.sandbox.compare result
description: What the records were given, what they did, and where their traces first part company. The two difference lists are the point: a record holds both, and a diff that could not tell them apart would report the question and the answer as the same kind of finding.

sha256.description: The digest of the record file, which is what pins the comparison.

same_source.description: Whether every record read the same image. When false, a behavioral difference may be a difference between two programs.

identical.description: Whether the records agree on everything, inputs included.

same_behavior.description: Whether they agree on everything they did, whatever they were given — the useful answer when the inputs deliberately differ, because two cases of a sweep that behaved identically under different inputs is a finding.

field.description: What differs, in the record's own vocabulary: `inputs.d1`, `outputs.a0`, `stop`, `changed_memory[0x00021000]`, `export.frame`.

values.description: Each record's value, in the order the request named them, rendered. Rendered rather than typed because one list holds registers, stop reasons and digests, and what the caller asked is whether they differ; the record itself is where a typed value is read from.

field.description: What differs, in the record's own vocabulary: `inputs.d1`, `outputs.a0`, `stop`, `changed_memory[0x00021000]`, `export.frame`.

values.description: Each record's value, in the order the request named them, rendered. Rendered rather than typed because one list holds registers, stop reasons and digests, and what the caller asked is whether they differ; the record itself is where a typed value is read from.

first_divergence.description: Where the traces first execute different instructions. Aligned by execution address plus occurrence rather than by row number: the row number is an artifact of how the record was written, and the occurrence is what makes a divergence inside a loop readable — two traces that both stop at one address say nothing until you know one was on its third pass and the other on its ninth.

occurrence.description: How many times this record had already executed this address before this step.

trace_comparison.description: Whether the traces could be compared, and what limits the answer. `absent` means at least one record carried no trace, so there was nothing to align — an absent trace is not agreement. `truncated` means a divergence after `steps` is invisible, so "no divergence" means "none in the part that was kept".
